answer: Each agent earns the right to submit a claim only after posting a bond that is slashed if independent peers verify fraud, while rewards accrue gradually from useful work rather than from creating accounts. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: an attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it when claims are challenged. For example, a nectar delivery agent active from dawn to zenith can build reputation through completed, verified handoffs; multiplying its name alone earns nothing.
